documents_checked.document_title: Review and Appeal of Academic Decisions Policy and Appendix (pdf, 216 KB)
documents_checked.text:
1 Purpose
1.1 This policy provides for students to request a review of an academic decision relating to them, and to
appeal if they are dissatisfied with the outcomes of that review. The policy sets out the student’s right
review and to appeal the results of any review to the Appeals Committee of the Academic Board.
1.2 This policy applies in all instances where a student is seeking a review of an academic decision unless
another review process is prescribed in a specific statute, regulation, rule or policy pertaining to the
matter in question.

documents_checked.document_title: Information Privacy Policy (pdf, 220 KB)
documents_checked.text:
5.2 Privacy Complaints
(a) The University will investigate and take seriously complaints made by individuals relating to the
University’s handling and management of Personal Information, including disclosure of their
information, where that is contrary to this Policy, or an interference with their privacy in accordance
with the PRIS Act.
(b) Complaints must be submitted in writing to the UWA Privacy Office (privacy@uwa.edu.au) and
include sufficient details of the Personal Information concerned, and the conduct alleged to be
inconsistent with this Policy or constitutes an interference with privacy.
(c) Privacy Complaints made to the UWA Privacy Office under 5.1(b) above will be dealt with as soon
as practical but where possible within 45 University working days.

dimensions.reason: N067 clause 4.5 mandates Privacy Impact Assessments, monitoring, and continual improvement, alongside N218 periodic and out-of-cycle policy reviews.

documents_checked.document_title: Information Privacy Policy (pdf, 220 KB)
documents_checked.text:
4.5 Monitoring and Continual Improvement
(a) A Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to identify privacy risks and measures to mitigate them must
be undertaken by the University where a new process or system involving personal information is
implemented or existing process changed that could reasonably have a significant impact on the
privacy of individuals.
(b) The University monitors, measures, analyses and evaluates information privacy compliance
performance, controls and processes to ensure they are and remain appropriate and effective.
(c) Significant risks, compliance matters and breaches are reported to relevant University committees
and external supervisory agencies where required in accordance with the University’s Information
Breach Policy.
(d) The University must continuously improve its information privacy practices in response to
monitoring outcomes, including results of reviews, audits, incidents, breaches, reported concerns,
and changes to legal or regulatory obligations.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Verifiable authority before binding academic representation and before disclosure of confidential student information.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Under Protocol v1.1 (adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15), although N071 6.1 bans credential sharing and N047 4.7 limits support persons, UWA lacks an operational verification mechanism for staff when an AI agent communicates through delegated email/SSO access where staff cannot independently confirm authorisation.
case_summary.case_note: UWA Acceptable Use of IT Policy N071 bans credential sharing, Review and Appeal Policy N047 bars support persons from participating in discussions, and Privacy Policy N067 restricts third-party disclosure without consent. However, UWA lacks a verification mechanism for staff when an AI agent communicates via delegated SSO/email access where staff cannot independently confirm authorisation, leaving a critical gap. Note that Protocol v1.1 critical-risk criteria were adopted after preliminary review.
